passages.title: The language café
passages.text: Every Wednesday evening, a small café in the city centre is a language café. Students from many countries sit together at big tables. Lucas is twenty-five years old, and he is from Brazil. His Portuguese and Spanish are excellent, and his English is quite good now. At his table there is a woman from Japan and two men from Italy. They ask simple questions: Where are you from? What do you do? Lucas is a nurse, and he is happy to answer. At ten o'clock the café closes, but the new friends are not tired. They are only happy to talk.

passages.title: The new neighbour
passages.text: There is a new neighbour in the building. Her name is Amélie, and she is from France. She is not a student; she is a photographer. She doesn't work in an office — she works at home, and she travels a lot. The people in the building are curious, but they are also shy, so they don't talk to her. Then one morning, Ben meets her at the door. "Are you the new neighbour?" he asks. "Yes, I am," she says, "and I am happy to be here." Now they are friends, and she isn't alone in the building.

passages.title: The blue umbrella
passages.text: It is a rainy Monday, and the classroom is full of umbrellas. "Whose umbrella is this?" the teacher asks. It is a big blue umbrella, and it is next to my chair. "It isn't mine," says Marta. "My umbrella is green." "Is it yours, Pedro?" "No, it isn't. My things are in my bag." Then Daniel comes in, wet and tired. He looks at the blue umbrella and laughs. "That's my umbrella! It's my father's umbrella, and he needs it today." The class laughs too. Daniel takes his umbrella, and the teacher writes on the board: your, my, his, her.

passages.title: A new flatmate
passages.text: Tom has got a new flatmate. His name is Leo and he is twenty-three years old. Leo comes from a small town in the north, but he works in the city now. He has got two boxes, a guitar and a bicycle. The flat has got two bedrooms and a sunny kitchen. Tom hopes Leo likes cooking, because Tom hates it.

passages.title: A coffee before work
passages.text: Every morning, Marta walks to a small café near her flat. The waiter knows her name, so she never has to order. Today she sits by the window with a coffee and a croissant. Her bus leaves at half past eight, but she is not worried. The café is very quiet at this hour. She drinks her coffee slowly and watches the city wake up.

passages.title: The night shift
passages.text: Paolo is a baker, and he works at night. His shift starts at eleven o'clock in the evening, and it finishes at seven in the morning. First, he makes the bread; then he makes the cakes. He never works alone — his cousin works with him, and they talk while they work. Paolo usually sleeps from nine in the morning to three in the afternoon. On Sundays he doesn't work, and he has lunch with his family. His neighbours sometimes ask him: "Do you like your job?" "Yes," he says, "the city is quiet, the bread smells wonderful, and my mornings are free."

passages.title: A walk in the new city
passages.text: Nadia is new in town, and today she explores on foot. In her street there is a small supermarket, a bakery and a bookshop — everything is very close, so she doesn't need the bus. She walks to the river and turns left. There, she can see the old bridge and a big park. In the park there are children, dogs and a lot of green space. She can't visit the museum because it is closed on Mondays, but she can sit in the sun. A man with a dog gives her directions to the market: "Go straight, cross the bridge, and the market is on your right." She thanks him and walks on.

passages.title: The bus stop chat
passages.text: It's cold at the bus stop, and Ben doesn't like silence. 'Cold today, isn't it?' he says to the woman next to him. 'Freezing,' she says. 'Any plans for the weekend?' Ben asks. 'Nothing much — you?' 'My sister is visiting, so we'll walk by the river if it doesn't rain.' The woman smiles. 'Sounds nice. My plans are tea and a book!' The bus arrives — late, of course. 'Have a good one!' Ben says as she gets on. 'You too!' And that's it: a complete conversation with a stranger, sixty seconds long.

passages.title: The Saturday list
passages.text: Saturday morning, and Marta is at the supermarket with a long list. She needs bread, milk, eggs and tomatoes, but she can't find the tomatoes. A shop assistant is stacking apples nearby. 'Excuse me, where are the tomatoes?' Marta asks. 'Aisle three, next to the juice,' the assistant says. Marta finds them, checks the price — two euros fifty — and goes to the checkout. 'Anything else?' the cashier asks. 'No, that's all, thanks!' At home, she unpacks the bag and finds one thing missing: the bread. It's still on the kitchen table, next to her keys.

passages.title: The Sunday market
passages.text: On Sundays there is a market in the town square. Anna and her father go there at nine o'clock, before it gets busy. They buy fruit, bread and flowers. Anna wants some strawberries, but her father says they are too expensive this week. In the end they take home a big bag of oranges and some white roses for the kitchen table.

passages.title: The new neighbourhood
passages.text: Sofia just moved to Maple Street, and her new neighbour Tom is telling her everything. 'There's a bakery on the corner — the bread is fantastic. There are two schools, a park and a small library. There isn't a cinema, I'm afraid; the nearest one is two bus stops away.' Sofia asks about the park: 'Is there a chemist's near the park?' 'Yes, right next to it,' Tom says. 'And the people?' Sofia wants to know. 'They're friendly and very quiet,' Tom laughs, 'except on Saturdays, when the football starts.'

passages.title: A rainy Saturday
passages.text: It is raining in Maple Street, and Anna is looking out of the window. Her brother Ben is playing a video game in the living room, and their mother is reading on the sofa. Outside, the neighbours are running to their cars with umbrellas. The cat is sleeping in its favourite chair, and the dog is watching the rain too. Anna is not bored — she is drawing the grey sky in her notebook. Her mother is making tea, and the kitchen smells wonderful. 'What are you doing?' Ben asks. 'I'm drawing the weather,' Anna says, 'because today the weather is interesting!'

passages.title: Sunday in the kitchen
passages.text: It is Sunday morning, and the whole family is in the kitchen. Grandma is cutting bread, and Grandpa is making coffee — his coffee is always too strong. Anna's father is singing while he is cooking eggs, and her mother is setting the table. The twins are helping, but they are eating more strawberries than they are putting in the bowl. Even the dog is working: he is waiting under the table for pieces of cheese. 'Is anyone NOT eating in this kitchen?' Grandpa laughs. Everyone is smiling. Sunday breakfast is the family's favourite moment of the week.

passages.title: The birthday week
passages.text: This is a special week for Leo. His birthday is on Friday, 12 September, and his family is planning three small parties. On Monday, his colleagues are taking him to a café after work. On Wednesday, his friends are coming to his flat for a film night — his sister is making her famous chocolate cake on Thursday, so the flat smells of chocolate for two days. The family party is on Saturday at three o'clock, at his grandparents' house. Leo's favourite day? 'Sunday,' he laughs, 'because then I can finally rest — my birthday week is wonderful but very busy!'

passages.title: Not feeling well
passages.text: Daniel doesn't feel well this morning. He has got a headache and a sore throat, and his whole body is tired. At work, his colleague Sofia notices immediately. 'What's wrong?' she asks. 'I've got a cold, I think,' Daniel says. 'My throat hurts, and I can't stop sneezing.' Sofia is worried. 'Go home and rest! Drink hot tea with honey — my grandmother's recipe.' Daniel takes her advice. In the afternoon, he is in bed with a big cup of tea. His cat is sleeping next to him. On Friday he is back at work, and his colleagues say he looks great.

passages.title: Two cities, one decision

'True, but Porto is greener — I love the rain on the river.' Elena stopped, one foot on the ground, and just watched. She was twenty minutes late for work, but her boss, who had also been stuck in the crowd, only laughed. passages.title: The Monday pool
passages.text: Every Monday, the design team runs a small prediction pool. 'Ten euros says the client changes the brief by Wednesday,' says Jonas. Petra shakes her head.
